title: Volumes store data outside a container
summary: A volume is storage managed separately from a container's writable layer. It can outlive a particular container.
introduction: A volume is storage managed separately from a container's writable layer. It can outlive a particular container. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain volumes store data outside a container
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A volume is storage managed separately from a container's writable layer. It can outlive a particular container.

blocks.code:
Container A writes a note to a named volume
Container A is removed
Container B mounts the same volume and reads the note
blocks.title: Volumes store data outside a container

blocks.text: The volume keeps data across container replacement. It still needs a backup plan for important data.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw which part is the container and which part holds lasting data.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A volume is not automatically a backup and is not deleted by removing only the container.
For more detail later, use this [Docker further reading](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/).

seo.title: Docker: Volumes store data outside a container
